text:
maia: FYI customer reported a weird provisioning gap after their SCIM sync — a handful of users lost the `admin` role even though they remain in the Okta group.

alex: Can you paste the error they saw or the time window?

maia: They saw several 403s in our SCIM connector logs around 2024-11-03T14:12Z. Error line: `403 insufficient_scope - token does not have groups.read` (redacted token id).

support-bot: (automated) Ticket CS-8271 created for customer AcmeCorp. Attach logs and repro steps.

tariq: That `insufficient_scope` comes from the upstream IdP call we make to Okta when expanding group members. If the OAuth token used by the SCIM connector lost the Groups scope, our group->role mapping step short-circuits and we end up not assigning role delta events.

lily: Did they rotate their OAuth credentials recently? Okta has a habit of reissuing tokens with narrower scopes when admins use the quick-app install.

maia: They said they rotated the app 2 days ago. We requested the admin who did it to confirm scopes.

alex: Repro strategy: create a test Okta app with same scopes minus `groups.read`, run a full sync against a test org, observe that group member expansion returns 403 and we fall back to creating users without role attachments.

tariq: Confirmed locally — reproed with minimal scopes. Patch from our SCIM-sync service shows this behavior:
```
2024-11-03T14:12:01Z scim-sync ERROR fetchGroupMembers groupId=00g1a2b3 403 insufficient_scope
2024-11-03T14:12:01Z scim-sync WARN roleMapSkipped userCount=6 group=admins
```

lily: That log line looks right. Two ways to fix: (1) have customer re-grant the OAuth app `groups.read` (or equivalent) so connector can expand memberships, then trigger a full resync; or (2) run a targeted repair job that queries Okta API using an elevated token and emits the missing role assignments (we can only do this with customer consent).

maia: Customer prefers a one-off repair rather than reconfiguring their app mid-day. They gave consent for us to run the targeted repair.

alex: Steps I'll run:
1) Validate current connector token scopes via `GET /oauth2/v1/introspect` (okta) — look for `groups.read`
2) If absent, fetch group membership for affected groups using their admin-provided elevated token (TLS+KMS check)
3) Emit role assignment events into our provisioning pipeline for the missing users
4) Kick an on-demand SCIM resync and monitor logs for roleMapSkipped warnings

tariq: For the repair job, watch for rate limits. The customer's tenant has ~12k users in the org. We should page groups and backoff on 429s. Also, make sure we sign the audit entry with the customer's consent text.

maia: I'll send them the consent doc and request a scoped token with `groups.read` or a temporary admin token for the repair.

lily: One small code mitigation we can ship: emit a specific alert when `roleMapSkipped` happens due to `insufficient_scope` and include an inline remediation link in the Console (how to re-grant scopes in Okta). That'll reduce MTTI. Can we scope that as a console bugfix?

alex: Yes — I'll open a small PR for the alert + mitigation copy. Low risk.

maia: Customer provided token (temp) at 2024-11-03T16:05Z. Alex ran the repair job and reports: "repair applied, 8 missing admin assignments re-added, no 429s, resync completed."

support-bot: (automated) CS-8271 status updated: Investigating -> Resolved (pending customer confirmation).

maia: Customer confirmed that previously locked users regained admin privs. They asked why it didn't auto-recover when the connector token was rotated.

tariq: Because when the token lacked groups permission, our sync only upserts users and skips group-member expansion — that step is non-idempotent in the presence of missing group data. The connector didn't mark the sync as failed — it treated it as a partial success. We'll update the status semantics so missing scopes surface as a sync failure.

lily: Good call. Also document the required scopes in our SCIM setup guide more prominently: `groups.read` (or the IdP equivalent), `users.read`, and `scim.manage` (whatever customer uses).

maia: Filing followups:
- GH issue for alert/console copy: RD-cc-1456 (alex)
- Backend change to mark sync failure on insufficient scopes: RD-cc-1457 (tariq)
- Docs update for SCIM required scopes: RD-cc-1458 (lily)

alex: I'll also add a short blurb to the repair playbook we use for escalations so support can offer the targeted repair option quickly.

maia: Thanks everyone. Closing thread after docs + alert PR merged and customer confirms stable over next 48h. :white_check_mark:
